candidate: On the first >=64 KiB unsent suffix on an owner without a loan, keep the consumed scratch buffer on that direction with its write offset and switch scratch buffers. Allocate at most one extra 256 KiB buffer per owner lazily, retaining it until owner destruction. Concurrent stalled streams and smaller suffixes continue to copy their exact remaining length.
method: One background-QoS thread on anonymous AF_UNIX streams. Each invocation runs a roomy 1 MiB and then a pressured 32 KiB downstream socket-buffer scenario, 4 established streams, 48 waves and 96 MiB verified per scenario. Every wave offers two 256 KiB payloads per stream. One fresh staged handshake and bidirectional exchange is submitted after the first owner pass. Its delay includes socketpair creation and the loaded owner until the first response is read. One warmup per arm and 16 alternating ABBA/BAAB blocks. Each block pools both invocations per arm. Intervals bootstrap the 16 whole blocks. Primary metric is owner CPU seconds per verified GiB under pressure. Verified MiB/s uses full wave wall time including seeding, comparison and the short exchanges. One thread cannot model arrivals during a running callback. Socket setup for fresh exchanges stages connect readiness. There is no IP, TCP, libdispatch scheduler, worker, or VM. Clock and heap/copy/write counters are equal in both arms.
qualification: Both variants passed ASan/UBSan in measurement and dedicated ownership controls: simultaneous blocked streams, zero and positive short writes, stalled-lease revocation and reuse while sibling data survives, small suffix fallback, and in-order data/FIN plus reverse traffic. Candidate also falls back to ordinary copying after failure to allocate its alternate buffer.
